diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma involving the CNS
legend: Cerebrospinal fluid cytological preparation. Cytology smear shows medium-sized lymphocytes with mild pleomorphism and conspicuous nucleoli (Giemsa).

diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma involving small intestine: growth patterns
legend: The central portion of the tumour shows dense transmural infiltration by lymphoma, with no overt necrosis. The mucosa shows loss or reduction of villi (<<30871>>). Extensive horizontal mucosal spread of lymphoma is present in the peripheral zone (<<30872>>).

diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma involving the small intestine
legend: There is a dense monomorphic infiltrate of lymphoma cells in the mucosa. There is marked epitheliotropism, with many neoplastic cells infiltrating the surface epithelium.

diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma involving small intestine: characteristic epitheliotropism
legend: The villi show prominent intraepithelial lymphocytosis in the mucosa distant from the tumour. Unlike in coeliac disease, villi are not atrophic, crypt hyperplasia is not seen, and there is no increase in plasma cells (<<30994>>). The lymphoma cells show positive immunostaining for CD3, which highlights the marked epitheliotropism (<<30971>>).

diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma: cytological spectrum
legend: Most frequently encountered are small to medium-sized cells with round or slightly irregular nuclei and dense chromatin (<<30975>>). Less frequently, medium-sized cells are admixed with occasional larger cells (<<30987>>).

diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma: cytological spectrum
legend: An example with a predominance of medium-sized cells with round or slightly irregular nuclei and lightly eosinophilic cytoplasm.

legend: The tumour cells are positive for CD8 (<<30990>>), CD56 (<<30991>>), and TIA1 (<<30992>>). They are usually also positive for TCRγ (<<30993>>), although rare cases express TCRβ instead, express both TCRγ and TCRβ, or express neither.
